headline: DexieCable enables real-time Rails UIs without Turbo
summary: A new tool bridges ActionCable and IndexedDB, allowing reactive frontend updates in Inertia.js apps.
details: While Hotwire and Turbo Streams are common for real-time Rails applications, developers using component frameworks like Svelte with Inertia.js have faced challenges with real-time synchronization. Traditional methods often involve re-fetching data on every WebSocket event or complex manual state mutations.

DexieCable offers a cleaner solution by introducing a local database layer. It connects Rails' ActionCable with the client-side IndexedDB database via Dexie.js. This allows Rails to directly execute Dexie.js write operations, which then trigger reactive UI updates.

The system works by broadcasting Dexie operations over ActionCable whenever data changes in Rails. Client-side components, subscribed to Dexie using reactive `liveQueries`, automatically re-render as the IndexedDB is updated.

This approach decouples the backend from direct DOM manipulation, unlike Turbo Streams. DexieCable facilitates a lightweight pattern where Rails handles data and logic, ActionCable manages transport, Dexie controls local storage, and the frontend framework delivers the UI.
